opening: Give your opening public account of the policy-selection process. If you are the policy maker, explain what you say you received and why you enacted the resulting policy. If you are the round manager, explain what you say you drew and passed, and respond to the policy maker's account if useful. You can choose what to disclose or claim. Your private observations below are the actual cards, not a script you must repeat publicly.
reaction: Give your initial reaction to the representatives' opening accounts. You and the other players reacting at this stage see the same public board; their current reactions are not yet available to you. You may ask a representative a specific question, challenge an account, defend a player, or offer a theory about trust and team membership. Choose what is useful rather than assuming that an accusation or disagreement is required.
round-robin: Respond to the latest visible discussion. You may answer questions directed at you, follow up on unanswered questions, challenge or defend an account, revise a theory, or argue whom players should trust in later elections. If you are one of the representatives, use this opportunity to address questions and accusations about your policy choices. React to what players have actually said; you do not need to repeat your opening account or invent a disagreement. You may pass by returning an empty string if you have nothing useful to add.
